question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten
question.problem: Ashley has $5$ tasks. She decides to do one on Thursday and another on Friday. How many different choices of the two tasks does Ashley have?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $5$ tasks to choose from, so $n=5.$ We want to select $2$ of those for Ashley to do, so we have $r=2.$ 

Therefore, the number of different choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{5}{P}_{2} & =\frac{5!}{(5-2)!} \\  & =\frac{5!}{3!} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 4\cdot \cancel{3!}}{\cancel{3!}} \\  & =5\cdot 4 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem: A bag contains $9$ different colored marbles. Jamie takes $4$ marbles from the bag, one at a time, and puts them in the order they were taken from the bag to create a sequence of colors. How many different sequences of colors are possible?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $9$ colored marbles, so $n=9.$ We want to select $4$ of those marbles to make a sequence of colors, so we have $r=4.$ 

Therefore, the number of different ways to choose the marbles is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{P}_{4} & =\frac{9!}{(9-4)!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{5!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}} \\  & =9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6 \\  & =3\,024.\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem: How many different arrangements of gold, silver, and bronze medalists can there be out of $10$ Olympic athletes, assuming there are no ties?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $10$ athletes, so $n=10.$ We want to select $3$ of those athletes to receive gold, silver, or bronze medals, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different ways to award the medals is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{10}{P}_{3} & =\frac{10!}{(10-3)!} \\  & =\frac{10!}{7!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot \cancel{7!}}{\cancel{7!}} \\  & =10\cdot 9\cdot 8 \\  & =720.\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem: How many $5$-letter words (legitimate or made-up) can be made using the letters of the word ALGORITHMS, where each letter cannot appear in the word more than once?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $10$ different letters in the word ALGORITHMS, so $n=10.$ We want to select $5$ of those letters to make a $5$-letter word, so we have $r=5.$

Therefore, the number of different made-up words is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{10}{P}_{5} & =\frac{10!}{(10-5)!} \\  & =\frac{10!}{5!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}} \\  & =10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6 \\  & =30\,240.\end{aligned}
$$
